The test image shows a tomato plant that has completely collapsed onto black plastic mulch. Key observations:
- Whole-plant wilt/collapse
- Plant is lying flat, likely detached or wilted at stem base
- Leaves still relatively intact (no major leaf spots)
- Left portion more severely affected/desiccated than right
- Sudden complete collapse pattern

This points to a vascular wilt or stem rot disease. Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.

The reference image shows a bacterial streaming test (diagnostic), confirming Bacterial_Wilt's rapid vascular colonization mechanism. The test image shows a tomato plant in complete sudden collapse on black plastic mulch with leaves still relatively intact (green, no major spotting) — this rapid whole-plant wilting without prior yellowing/lesions is the hallmark of Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum). Southern Blight would show white mycelium/sclerotia at the stem base; Sclerotinia would show stem lesions; Verticillium causes slower, more gradual decline.
